chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan, from Al-Qasim, from Aban, from Ismail Al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'If a man kills another man intentionally,' he said, 'He must perform three expiations: freeing a slave, fasting for two consecutive months, and feeding sixty poor people.' And he said, 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) issued a fatwa to the same effect.'

key_terms.أَفْتَى: Issued a legal ruling or fatwa
key_terms.كَفَّارَاتٍ: Expiations or compensations for a sin or error

ai.seo_question: What are the three expiations for intentional murder in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam establishes the triad of expiations for intentional homicide, linking the juristic authority of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir with the precedent set by Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin). The inclusion of the Imam's fatwa underscores the continuity of legal reasoning within the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing that these specific compensations serve as both spiritual purification and social restitution in Shia fiqh.
